answer: Voting power is capped per identity, so even if an attacker controls thousands of accounts each one can only influence a verdict by a tiny fixed amount, and the total is still limited by how much genuine, recent work the cluster can honestly submit. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a terrace as the anchor of the cost.
